claims.text: The starting eutectic high-entropy alloy has a dual-phase lamellar structure, typically FCC plus B2.
Low-temperature annealing immediately after casting or solution treatment induces short-range atomic ordering.
The proposed low-temperature anneal refines or otherwise beneficially adjusts eutectic lamellar spacing.
The proposed anneal enhances coherence at the interfaces between the eutectic phases.
Short-range ordering within the soft phase causes the refined lamellar spacing and enhanced phase-interface coherence.
The annealing-induced changes strengthen phase boundaries and increase dislocation blocking.
The annealing-induced interfacial changes delay crack initiation.
The treatment maintains sufficient connectivity of the constituent phases.
Maintaining phase connectivity and reducing stress concentrations preserves or improves ductility.
Relative to the as-cast baseline, the annealed alloy will show statistically significant increases in both yield strength and tensile elongation.
An optimized interplay between hard and soft phases produces a more balanced strength-ductility profile.
Conventional as-cast eutectic high-entropy alloys generally exhibit a strength-ductility trade-off.
The predicted effect should be observable in room-temperature tensile testing at standard strain rates.
Annealing below conventional aging temperatures for a limited duration can induce short-range ordering without extensive precipitation.
The simultaneous improvement requires annealing conditions that avoid excessive precipitation and lamellar coarsening.
AlCoCrFeNi-based compositions can support the required dual-phase lamellar eutectic structure.
The mechanism may not transfer to alloys with substantially different phase distributions.
TEM and diffraction-based measurements can establish the proposed changes in lamellar spacing, interfacial coherence, and short-range ordering.
Failure to obtain greater than 5% improvement in both strength and ductility together with the proposed microstructural changes is the stated falsification criterion.
